questions.stem: Under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, when must the master of a Canadian vessel (not on the small vessel register) make sure the Canadian flag is flown?
options: Only on Canada Day
When signalled to do so by a government vessel or Canadian Forces vessel, and when entering or leaving, or while moored or anchored in, a port
Only when in Canadian waters at night
Never, since flying it is optional
questions.explanation: Section 64 requires the flag to be flown when signalled by a government vessel or a vessel under Canadian Forces command, and when entering or leaving, or while moored at or anchored in, a port. It is not limited to a holiday or to Canadian waters, and it is not optional.

questions.stem: Which vessel must carry a set of International Code of Signals flags under the Navigation Safety Regulations?
options: A 12 m Canadian pleasure craft in sheltered waters
Every vessel of any size
A Canadian vessel of 200 GT on a near coastal Class 1 voyage
A 100 GT tug on an inland voyage
questions.explanation: Every Canadian vessel of more than 150 GT on a near coastal Class 1 or unlimited voyage must carry the set of signal flags. A small pleasure craft, a 100 GT tug, or 'every vessel' does not fit the rule.

options: A: I am taking in dangerous goods; B: I have a diver down
A: man overboard; B: all persons report on board
A: I require a pilot; B: I have a pilot on board
A: I have a diver down, keep well clear at slow speed; B: I am taking in, discharging or carrying dangerous goods
questions.explanation: A means 'I have a diver down; keep well clear at slow speed' and B means 'I am taking in, or discharging, or carrying dangerous goods'. Swapping them is the common slip. A pilot is G (or H when one is on board), man overboard is O and the report-on-board call is P.

questions.stem: Two trawlers in a fleet, close together on the fishing grounds, each hoist flag Z. What does it mean among fishing vessels there?
options: I am pair trawling
I require a tug
I am hauling nets
I am shooting nets
questions.explanation: Among fishing vessels close together on the fishing grounds, Z means 'I am shooting nets'. In other settings Z means 'I require a tug', G means 'I require a pilot' (and among fishing vessels 'I am hauling nets'), and T means pair trawling.

questions.stem: In harbour, a ship hoists flag P. What should the crew do?
options: Leave the ship
All persons should report on board, as the vessel is about to proceed to sea
Treat it as a request for a pilot
Hoist flag Q at once
questions.explanation: In harbour, flag P calls all persons to report on board because the vessel is about to proceed to sea. Q is the request for free pratique (the ship is healthy), and a pilot request is G.

options: E means 'dragging anchor' and I means 'fire'
E means 'altering to port' and I means 'altering to starboard'
E means 'altering course to starboard' and I means 'altering course to port'
E means 'stopped' and I means 'astern'
questions.explanation: E is 'I am altering my course to starboard' and I is 'I am altering my course to port'. S is 'I am operating astern propulsion' and M is 'my vessel is stopped and making no way'. Y is dragging.

questions.stem: A ship at anchor hoists flag Y. What is she telling nearby vessels?
options: I have a diver down
I require medical assistance
I am disabled
I am dragging my anchor
questions.explanation: Y means 'I am dragging my anchor'. Disabled is F, diver down is A and medical assistance is W.

questions.stem: Match the signal to its meaning: which statement is correct?
options: J: free pratique; W: pair trawling; V: stop your vessel
J: on fire with dangerous cargo, keep well clear; W: I require medical assistance; V: I require assistance
J: man overboard; W: I have a pilot; V: keep clear
J: I am taking in stores; W: wind warning; V: vessel stopped
questions.explanation: J means 'I am on fire and have dangerous cargo on board: keep well clear of me' (or leaking dangerous cargo), W means 'I require medical assistance' and V means 'I require assistance'. O is man overboard, H is pilot on board, Q is free pratique, T is pair trawling and L is 'stop your vessel instantly'.

questions.stem: Which description is correct for D, F and U?
options: D: keep clear, I am manoeuvring with difficulty; F: I am disabled, communicate with me; U: you are running into danger
D: diver down; F: fire; U: underway
D: I am disabled; F: keep clear, manoeuvring with difficulty; U: stop instantly
D: dragging; F: free pratique; U: under tow
questions.explanation: D is 'keep clear of me; I am manoeuvring with difficulty', F is 'I am disabled; communicate with me' and U is 'you are running into danger'. Swapping D and F is the common slip, and the last two options invent meanings.

questions.stem: Which spellings are used in the phonetic alphabet for the letters A and J?
options: Alfa and Juliet
Alfa and Juliett
Able and Jig
Alpha and Juliet
questions.explanation: The spelling alphabet uses Alfa (not Alpha) and Juliett (with two t's). Able and Jig belong to an older wartime alphabet.
